cues.text: Let's make something in Podor.
Press Control N to open a new canvas.
Set the width to twelve hundred pixels, and the height to nine hundred. Create your canvas, and start with a clean page.
Open the color panel and enter a Bordeaux red.
Choose Ink. Increase the size, then draw a continuous line across the canvas.
Switch to Soft for a diffused edge.
Now try Marker. The same movement produces a different finish. Compare the three marks before choosing your brush.
Open Color. Drag around the ring to choose a hue, then move inside the square to adjust brightness and saturation.
Add this color to your palette. Choose another swatch and save that too, ready for your next stroke.
Here is a layered study. Toggle the foreground off and on to see how the image is built.
Duplicate the active layer, then open its blending controls.
Try Multiply and watch the colors deepen. Return to Normal, and confirm the result.
Press M and drag a rectangle around part of the painting.
Copy the visible selection with Control Shift C. Paste it onto a new layer, then clear the selection with Control D.
Press Control T to transform the pasted layer.
Drag the artwork into position, then press Enter to apply the move.
Use Undo to step back through the move and the paste. The original composition is still there.
Open Adjust, then Curves.
Add a point and lift the curve. Watch the active layer brighten as you drag.
Toggle the preview to compare with the original. Apply the change when the balance feels right.
Copy a reference image, then press Control Shift V to place it on the canvas.
Drag it beside your work. Pull a corner to resize it without changing its proportions.
References stay separate from the painting. They will not appear in your export, and are kept only for this session.
Open Export to prepare the finished image.
Choose JPEG for a flat image, or PSD for supported pixel layers.
For this study, choose PNG and export. The reference stays out of the final image.
Save the editable project, then return home. Your recent work is ready to open again.
From the first mark to the finished piece. Podor.
